title: Lesson Plan — Acids, Bases and Salts (Class 10 CBSE Science)
subject: Science
objectives: Distinguish acids and bases by indicator behaviour.
Predict and balance reactions of acids with metals, carbonates, and metal oxides.
Predict and balance reactions of bases with non-metallic oxides and acids (neutralisation).
Explain the role of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions; distinguish strong vs weak.
Use the pH scale to classify and compare solutions.
Apply pH knowledge to real situations (tooth decay, acid rain, soil, stings).
Identify common salts (NaOH, NaHCO₃, Na₂CO₃, CaOCl₂, plaster of Paris) and their uses.
prerequisites: Chapter 1 — types of reactions (esp. acid + metal as displacement; acid-base neutralisation).
Familiarity with chemical formulas and balanced equations.
materials: Phenolphthalein and methyl orange indicator solutions
Reagent bottles: dilute HCl, NaOH, Ca(OH)₂ (lime water), CuO, Zn granules

activities.description: Hook with a kitchen demonstration. Add a few drops of phenolphthalein to soap water — it turns pink. Then add a little lemon juice — pink fades to colourless. Ask: what just happened?
Pair activity: students test 6 household substances (lemon juice, vinegar, soap solution, tap water, baking soda, sugar) with red AND blue litmus. They classify each as acid / base / neutral.

Five blocks: (i) acids + bases vocabulary + indicators; (ii) the three acid reactions with examples; (iii) the three base reactions; (iv) H⁺/OH⁻ ions, strong vs weak, dilution safety; (v) pH scale + practical applications + salts (chlor-alkali, baking soda, plaster of Paris).
teacher_actions: Demonstrate Zn + HCl live (H₂ pop test).
Walk through pH chart with everyday examples.
Show CuSO₄·5H₂O blue → white on heating.
student_actions: Write balanced equations from word equations.

activities.description: Worksheet: 6 questions covering all the blocks.
Exit ticket — 6 questions covering each block.
Set homework: pH chart of 5 household substances + paragraph on tooth decay + chemical name of 4 common salts.
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter (Metals and Non-metals).

homework: Test the pH of 5 household substances (use universal indicator paper) and tabulate.
Write a paragraph (5-6 sentences) on 'How sugar leads to tooth decay'. Use the words: bacteria, acid, enamel, pH, toothpaste.
Write the chemical name and ONE use each of: common salt, baking soda, washing soda, plaster of Paris.
assessment_ideas: Use the 6-item exit ticket as formative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on chlor-alkali process using a 'reactions + uses' rubric.
Peer-grade the homework pH chart for accuracy and clear classification.
references: NCERT Class 10 Science textbook (jesc1dd), Chapter 2: Acids, Bases and Salts.
